title: Strings and picks he makes himself
summary: His preferred Gibson and wrapped-G strings, and the thick blunt picks he makes from toothbrush handles or comb backs.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Is there anything special about the strings that you like? Any certain brand or size or material or something?
Well, I like the Gibson string. I think the Gibson has as good a guitar string as any major.

Is that all pretty much, I was thinking about the guitar, I didn't ask intelligent questions on some of these, but are all the strings usually the same, or some of them wild and the top, the highest ones are they just a plain?

Well, they used to have the first three strings, the E, B, and G were steel, all steel. But now you have the rap G, the G is rap as well as the bass strings. And I always use rap G, I like them. Yeah. Yeah. I like the tone of them.
Anything special about your pick or anything?
Well, I use the very blunt pick. I make them out of toothbrush handles. Something real thick.
Something real thick.
Jude used to make his own out of bone. Yeah, not flexible.
No, no, they're not flexible at all.
It's hard. It has a taper on the end.
Yeah.
And it hits just like a finger.
Mm-hmm. Yeah. Solid.
And I can't use those slap picks. I can't keep them straight in my hand. They work this way.
I just can't hold them.
But then I get the other one in between my thumb and these fingers here, see. Yeah. And I can hold it all night.
You're a little bit bigger than some of those little ones? Do you make your picks bigger when you make them, or...? No, I see.
I have one of the answer you use. Yeah, sure.

Mm-hmm. Well, I see. It's only about less and a half an inch wide and just... Mm-hmm. ...about an inch long and tapered. Yeah. And it's almost about three sixteenths of an inch thick. Yeah, it's about. Yeah.
Just depending on the material I had. Sometimes it's a little thicker.
I thought it might be easier to hold it, even make it bigger than that or something, make a big grip.
Well, it would be. It would be. It just depends on, as I said, it depends on the material. This was made of the back of a comb.
Oh, yeah. I see. Yeah.
It was narrow. So I used it just as it was. But it's still, I still get a good grip on it, you see. Oh, yeah, sure. It's between my thumb and these two fingers.
Yeah. First finger then braced against your second finger.
That's right. That's what I use. Mm-hmm. And when you hit, you hit like... That's why the bases ring out, so I hit it solid, you know.
Oh, yeah.
Mm-hmm.
